claims.text: SACU’s established common customs arrangements and shared revenue mechanism are practical forms of cooperation, rather than merely a declaration of friendship. They can ease internal goods trade and provide public revenue. Dependence on customs receipts exposes budgets to changes in that revenue, while the much larger South African economy creates unequal productive capacities within the union. SADC has created regional institutions and a free-trade framework among participating states. These provide routes for cooperation but do not remove every border delay, transport bottleneck or political disagreement. Unequal infrastructure and capacity can make gains uneven. Distinguish an institution or agreement that exists from the size of its economic effect, which needs dated performance evidence.

claims.text: The 2016 EU–SADC Economic Partnership Agreement illustrates a regional trade relationship involving Namibia. Market-access arrangements can support exporters and encourage coordination, but firms still need to meet applicable standards and deliver reliably. Compliance can be costly for smaller producers; competition can benefit buyers while placing pressure on some local firms. An agreement’s existence is an achievement of cooperation, not evidence that all products or producers gain equally.
